title: The Americas at the World Cup
description: CONMEBOL and CONCACAF — the Americas have produced some of the World Cup's greatest nations, moments and rivalries.

questions.q: CONMEBOL nations have won the most World Cup titles of any confederation. How many titles have South American nations won in total?
questions.explain: South American nations have won 10 World Cups: Brazil 5 (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002), Argentina 3 (1978, 1986, 2022) and Uruguay 2 (1930, 1950). No other confederation comes close.

questions.q: Brazil is the only nation to have qualified for every single World Cup. How many tournaments have they entered since 1930?
questions.explain: Brazil have qualified for all 22 World Cups from 1930 to 2022 — the only nation with a 100% qualification record. This extraordinary consistency is unmatched in world football.

questions.q: The USA hosted the 1994 World Cup and set attendance records. Which European nation won that tournament?
questions.explain: Brazil beat Italy on penalties in the 1994 final — the first World Cup final decided by a shootout. Roberto Baggio famously missed the decisive penalty for Italy. The 1994 USA World Cup set attendance records that stood for decades.

questions.q: Mexico's 'Quinto Partido' (fifth match) curse refers to their exit at the same stage for seven consecutive World Cups. Which stage?
questions.explain: Mexico were eliminated in the round of 16 — the fifth match — in 1994, 1998, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014 and 2018. The 'Quinto Partido' curse became a national obsession, finally broken when Mexico failed to reach the round of 16 in 2022.

questions.q: The USA's best World Cup result is third place at the inaugural 1930 tournament. They also made history in 1950. What did they do?
options: Beat England 1–0 in one of the greatest upsets
Reached the semi-finals for a second time
questions.explain: The USA beat England 1–0 in the 1950 group stage — one of the greatest World Cup upsets ever. Joe Gaetjens scored the winner. The match was dubbed the 'Miracle on Grass' and remains one of American football's finest moments.

questions.q: The 2026 World Cup is co-hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico — the first ever three-nation World Cup. How many total matches will be played?
questions.explain: The 2026 World Cup will feature 104 matches — up from 64 at 32-team tournaments — due to the expansion to 48 teams and 12 groups. The three co-hosts will share games across 16 venues in 11 cities.

questions.q: Argentina's 2022 World Cup win ended a 36-year drought. Who scored the winning penalty in the final shootout?
questions.explain: Gonzalo Montiel scored the decisive penalty to win Argentina the 2022 World Cup — the same player who had fouled Mbappé to give France their third goal. Montiel's penalty gave Argentina a 4–2 shootout win after a 3–3 draw.

questions.q: Which CONCACAF nation caused the biggest upset at the 2022 World Cup — knocking out a European powerhouse?
questions.explain: The USA drew with England and beat Iran in 2022 — a strong showing. However, the biggest CONCACAF upset belongs to Saudi Arabia (AFC) and, arguably, the consistent surprise of Mexico's elimination despite a famous opening win (in this case, Mexico failed to advance from their group).

questions.q: Colombia has qualified for consecutive World Cups in the 21st century. Which player inspired them to qualify unbeaten for 2014?
questions.explain: Falcao led Colombia's qualifying campaign for 2014, scoring throughout. He then suffered a serious knee injury in January 2014 and missed the tournament itself. Colombia still excelled with James Rodríguez winning the Golden Boot.

questions.q: The 2026 World Cup final is scheduled at which venue — making North America the ninth region to host a World Cup final?
questions.explain: MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — the home stadium of the New York Giants and Jets — is scheduled to host the 2026 World Cup final. The stadium holds 82,500 and is one of the NFL's largest venues.
